britannica.rawText:
WOR                    [ 930 ]                    WOR

WORMWOOD. See ARTEMISIA.
  WORMS, in medicine, are of three principal kinds
found in the human body: the round worm, or lumbri-
cus; the ſmall thread-worm, or aſcaris, which lodges
in the lower gut; and the tape-worm, or tænia, which
is flat and jointed, and ſometimes many yards long.
  Children are much more ſubject to worms than grown
perſons, eſpecially thoſe who eat much fruit and un-
ripe food. Some have held that worms are bred from
the corruption of the humours in the bowels; but it is
more probable that they come from eggs ſwallowed
with our food and drink.
  The ſigns of worms are a pale countenance, itching
of the noſe, grinding of the teeth in ſleep, a ſwelled
belly, and an appetite ſometimes craving and ſome-
times wanting. Of the remedies, the moſt approved are
mercury, powder of tin, and the down of cowhage mixed
with ſyrup, followed by a purge.
  The tape-worm is the moſt difficult to expel, and if
the head be not brought away, it grows again.
  WORSHIP, the outward expreſſion of reverence

passages.text: WORMS, in medicine, are of three principal kinds found in the human body: the round worm, or lumbricus; the small thread-worm, or ascaris, which lodges in the lower gut; and the tape-worm, or taenia, which is flat and jointed, and sometimes many yards long.
Children are much more subject to worms than grown persons, especially those who eat much fruit and unripe food.
Some have held that worms are bred from the corruption of the humours in the bowels; but it is more probable that they come from eggs swallowed with our food and drink.
The signs of worms are a pale countenance, itching of the nose, grinding of the teeth in sleep, a swelled belly, and an appetite sometimes craving and sometimes wanting.
Of the remedies, the most approved are mercury, powder of tin, and the down of cowhage mixed with syrup, followed by a purge.
The tape-worm is the most difficult to expel, and if the head be not brought away, it grows again.
Helminthiasis, also known as worm infection, is any disease of humans or animals caused by parasitic worms, or helminths. The main groups are roundworms, tapeworms and flukes.

Soil-transmitted helminths include the large roundworm Ascaris lumbricoides, whipworm and hookworm. The pinworm, Enterobius vermicularis, lives in the large intestine and causes itching around the anus.

Most worms spread when their eggs, passed in the faeces of an infected person, contaminate soil, water or food and are swallowed. Tapeworms are mostly caught by eating undercooked meat or fish containing larvae.
Worm infections are among the most common infections in the world. They mostly affect children in poor regions with little access to clean water and sanitation.
Light infections often cause no symptoms. Heavy infections can cause abdominal pain, diarrhoea, malnutrition, anaemia and poor growth in children.
Infections are treated with anthelmintic drugs such as albendazole, mebendazole and praziquantel. In many countries, school children are dewormed regularly.
A tapeworm attaches to the gut wall with its head, the scolex, and grows by adding segments. Treatment must kill or remove the head, or the worm can regrow.

reasons: The 1797 headword WORMS is a plain plural noun. The closest Wikipedia article uses the medical term Helminthiasis.
The general Worm article scores higher on embedding but is about worms as animals, so the reranker drops it.
Rerank 0.68 is below our 0.75 threshold for a strong match: Helminthiasis covers the topic, but no single article matches all three kinds the entry describes.

alignments.label: The round worm
alignments.note: Same worm. Its old name, lumbricus, survives in the species name.

alignments.label: The thread-worm

britannica.quote: the small thread-worm, or ascaris, which lodges in the lower gut

wikipedia.quote: The pinworm, Enterobius vermicularis, lives in the large intestine

alignments.note: A change in language: in 1797 'ascaris' meant the thread-worm; today Ascaris is the large roundworm.

alignments.label: Flat and jointed

britannica.quote: the tape-worm, or taenia, which is flat and jointed

alignments.note: The 1797 joints are the modern segments.

alignments.label: Children most affected

britannica.quote: Children are much more subject to worms than grown persons

alignments.note: Same observation. Wikipedia ties it to poor sanitation, not to fruit.

alignments.label: Swallowed eggs

britannica.quote: they come from eggs swallowed with our food and drink

wikipedia.quote: contaminate soil, water or food and are swallowed

alignments.note: The 1797 entry already rejects the idea that worms breed from corruption, and picks the answer that holds today.

alignments.label: Signs of worms

britannica.quote: a pale countenance, itching of the nose, grinding of the teeth in sleep, a swelled belly

wikipedia.quote: Heavy infections can cause abdominal pain, diarrhoea, malnutrition, anaemia

alignments.note: Pallor and a swollen belly fit anaemia and heavy infection. Inference: the nose and teeth signs have no support in the Wikipedia text.

alignments.label: Mercury and tin

britannica.quote: mercury, powder of tin, and the down of cowhage

wikipedia.quote: anthelmintic drugs such as albendazole, mebendazole and praziquantel

alignments.note: The old remedies are replaced by drugs that kill the worms.

alignments.label: The head regrows

britannica.quote: if the head be not brought away, it grows again

wikipedia.quote: Treatment must kill or remove the head, or the worm can regrow

alignments.note: The same practical rule, two centuries apart.

alignments.label: Often silent

wikipedia.quote: Light infections often cause no symptoms

alignments.note: The 1797 entry lists signs but does not say that most infections show none.

alignments.label: Mass deworming
alignments.note: Treating whole groups at once is a modern public-health idea.

suggestedQuestions: Did the 1797 entry know where worms come from?
Does 'ascaris' mean the same worm in 1797 and today?

Did the 1797 entry know where worms come.answer: Mostly, yes. The 1797 entry mentions the old view that worms breed from corruption in the bowels, but judges it more probable that they come from eggs swallowed with food and drink [B3]. Wikipedia says most worms spread when eggs from faeces contaminate soil, water or food and are swallowed [W3].

Does 'ascaris' mean the same worm in 179.answer: No. In 1797 'ascaris' is the small thread-worm of the lower gut [B1]. Today that worm is the pinworm, Enterobius vermicularis, and Ascaris names the large roundworm [W2]. This is a change in language, not in knowledge: both texts describe the same two worms.

How were worms treated in 1797?.answer: With mercury, powder of tin and the down of cowhage in syrup, followed by a purge [B5]. Today anthelmintic drugs such as albendazole, mebendazole and praziquantel are used [W6]. One rule survives: a tapeworm grows again unless its head is removed [B6] [W7].
